truth.affected_span_verbatim: Because $k$ is a real-valued rank rather than a bit-width, ExTernD's accuracy/cost trade-off is instead continuous: the inner-rank multiplier $\mu$ (storage and compute both scale linearly with it, Sec.~\ref{sec:cost}) and a sparsity threshold $\tau$ (which sets the fraction of zeros in $B$ and $C$, e.g.\ $\tau{=}0.7 \to {\sim}41\%$ zeros, $\tau{=}1.0 \to {\sim}57\%$, $\tau{=}2.0 \to {\sim}87\%$) can each be set per matrix to any real value, letting a target accuracy be hit exactly rather than rounded up to the next bit-width.
